prompt: On a toy prime-field curve modulo 17, evaluating a candidate point gives 1 on the left of the curve equation and an unreduced value of 137 on the right. Is the point on the curve?

options.text: No: 1 and 137 must be identical integers.
options.explanation: Finite-field membership compares remainders, not unreduced integers.
Both sides have the same remainder, satisfying the curve relation.

options.text: No: the right side is larger than the modulus.
options.explanation: Intermediate integers may exceed the modulus before reduction.

options.text: Yes: every coordinate pair is automatically on any curve.
options.explanation: Only pairs satisfying the particular curve equation are points.

workedExample:
1. Divide 137 by 17. Eight full groups account for 136, leaving 1.
2. The left side also has remainder 1.
3. The modular curve relation therefore holds for this candidate. Membership alone does not prove a point has a suitable subgroup order for a real protocol.
